Question B-003-013-005.

Why the correct answer is right: FM is useful locally on VHF/UHF because a sufficiently strong carrier gives quiet, readable audio even at modest signal levels.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "It provides a good signal-to-noise ratio at low RF signal levels": This is the correct choice because FM is useful locally on VHF/UHF because a sufficiently strong carrier gives quiet, readable audio even at modest signal levels.
- sourceIndex 1: "The carrier is not detectable": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from It provides a good signal-to-noise ratio at low RF signal levels. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, carrier terminology is being applied to the wrong modulation condition here.
- sourceIndex 2: "It is more resistant to distortion caused by reflected signals": This answer would fit a different fault than It provides a good signal-to-noise ratio at low RF signal levels. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Its RF carrier stays on frequency better than the AM modes": This option confuses another station topic with It provides a good signal-to-noise ratio at low RF signal levels. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, carrier terminology is being applied to the wrong modulation condition here.
